package_info.package_versions: Electron Windows and Mac desktop app versions distributed in March 2023 (exact versions not specified in report)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CX Desktop App was compromised via a supply chain attack, where threat actors inserted malicious JavaScript code into the official Electron app update. This code enabled the download and execution of arbitrary payloads from attacker-controlled infrastructure, resulting in remote command execution, malware installation, and the potential for widespread compromise of user systems through a trusted software channel.

execution_context.trigger: At application launch or immediately after update installation
execution_context.file_location: Electron app bundle main process JavaScript file (e.g., main.js or a loaded module within the app's asar archive)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At application launch or immediately after update installation, the code initiates an outbound network request to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, downloads a binary payload, writes the payload to disk as 'payload.exe', and executes it as a new process, resulting in remote code execution and enabling further compromise of the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs an unsolicited download of an executable from an external, non-3CX domain and immediately executes it, which is a hallmark of supply chain attacks and is never expected in legitimate update or runtime logic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Electron app code should only download updates from official, signed sources and must verify code signatures before execution. It should never fetch and execute unsigned binaries from third-party domains without user consent or validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may download signed update packages from official vendor servers and verify their integrity before installation, but they do not download and execute arbitrary binaries from untrusted, non-official domains.
key_indicators: Hardcoded network request to a non-3CX domain within main process JavaScript
Creation of a new executable file (e.g., payload.exe) in the app directory at runtime
Immediate execution of the downloaded binary without signature verification
Absence of user notification or consent for the download and execution
No code integrity or authenticity checks on the downloaded payload

attack_chain.action: Threat actors compromise the 3CX software supply chain, gaining access to the build environment and injecting malicious code into the Electron app source.
attack_chain.leads_to: Insertion of malicious JavaScript code into the 3CX app update package

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript code is distributed to users via the official 3CX update channels as part of the Electron app bundle.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code on user endpoints upon app launch or update

attack_chain.action: Upon installation or launch, the injected code in the 3CX app downloads a secondary payload from an attacker-controlled domain and writes it to disk.
attack_chain.leads_to: Presence of attacker-supplied executable on the victim system

attack_chain.action: The downloaded payload is executed, granting the attacker remote code execution capabilities and enabling further malicious actions such as data theft or additional malware deployment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of affected systems and potential lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Electron app main process initiating outbound network requests to non-3CX domains at runtime
Unexpected creation and execution of new binaries (e.g., payload.exe) by the 3CX app process
App update or launch event followed by process creation of unsigned executables
file_indicators: Presence of fetch or network request code to unknown domains in Electron app main process files (main.js, preload.js, or modules within app.asar)
Newly created executable files (e.g., payload.exe) appearing in the 3CX app directory after update or launch
Modified or unexpected JavaScript code within the app.asar archive
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from the 3CX app to domains not owned or operated by 3CX (e.g., malicious-domain.com)
Download of executable content (application/octet-stream) from non-official sources during or after app update
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Electron-based applications, especially 3CX Desktop App, for unexpected outbound network requests to non-official domains during or after updates. Inspect main process JavaScript files and app.asar archives for injected fetch or download logic targeting unknown domains. Alert on the creation and execution of new, unsigned binaries by the app process. Correlate update or launch events with subsequent process creation and network activity to identify potential supply chain compromise.
